d. Takeout includes the share manifest + erasure log (portability + accountability).

**DEPENDENCY RULING (Alex): the core chain is explicit and lives in the graph as depends_on edges.** TICKETS depend on DOCS (specs, wikified tickets, proof pages all land in BB Docs — BBT without a working doc store is half a tracker); the WIKI depends on the WORKER (integral per today's 1479 ruling — no treatment, no wiki); CORPUS depends on both (folder → worker treatment → embed). Register the edges: bbt —depends_on→ bbdocs; bbdocs-wiki —depends_on→ wiki-worker; corpus-module —depends_on→ {bbdocs, wiki-worker, vectorize}. Consequences the graph must answer: (1) possibility()/context_pack cite the dependency chain when a build touches any link of it; (2) the WATERFALL CASCADES — a dependency down shows its dependents degraded-by-dependency (named: "degraded: wiki-worker down"), never independently green; (3) deploy/teardown ordering respects the edges (never ship a dependent ahead of its substrate); (4) the backup law (2512) prioritizes by dependency depth — the stores most depended-upon back up first. This is the general rule, not just these three: every service registers its depends_on edges at landing, and an edge-less service with obvious dependencies is a lint finding.

Three computed views over the edges: transitive closure → waterfall cascade ("degraded: X down"); topological sort of hard edges → deploy order; depth count → backup priority (2512). And CONFIRMED, the circle Alex named: **Payload config is built via template FROM the graph** — graph rows (field specs, policy rows, dependency edges) are the source, the payload-collection template stamps the config, the admin UI materializes over it. The graph describes; templates stamp; Payload renders. Nothing configured by hand twice — the graph is the single declaration point, and the dependency edges are just more rows the same templates can read.
